sentences.text:
The petitioner a private limited company, engaged in the business of exporting processed sea foods,
imported a consignment of Sodium Tri Poly Phosphate as per bill of entry No.3807012 dated 14.11.2013 from Belgium.

Since the goods were not found to conform to the standard laid down under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Commissioner of Customs issued Ext.P6 show cause notice dated 18.12.2013 calling upon the petitioner to show cause why the goods should not be confiscated.
The petitioner thereupon submitted Ext.P7 letter dated 26.12.2013 requesting the Commissioner to sent a sample to the Referral Laboratory.

A sample was accordingly sent to the Referral Laboratory which issued Ext.P11 analysis report dated 6.1.2014 to the effect that the sample does not conform to the standards laid down in the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thereupon, the petitioner submitted Ext.P12 representation dated 12.2.2014 before the Commissioner of Customs requesting him to waive the demurrage/detention charges accrued on the consignment, the penalty if any charged and also for permission to re-export the shipment at the earliest.

The instant writ petition was thereupon filed on 14.3.2014, seeking the following reliefs:-
"i) Call for the entire records pertaining to the Exhibit P3 and Exhibit P11 reports,
which form the ground for rejection of NOC by the 1st Respondent.
ii) Issue a writ of mandamus, any other writ, order or direction to the 1st Respondent to consider the Exhibit P 12 and allow re-export of the consignment.

2 iii) Issue a writ of mandamus, any other writ, order or direction, to declare that the test report conducted by the 2nd Respondent is improper and the demurrage/detention charges claimed by the 1st Respondent on the basis of proceedings initiated thereunder is against the principles of law.

sentences.text:
iv) Issue a writ of mandamus, any other writ, order or direction, to the 2nd Respondent to conduct a fresh test of the consignment in strict compliance with the provisions of The Food Safety and Standards (Food products standards and Food additives) Regulations 2011.
v) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other Writ, order direction to the 3rd and 4th Respondents to establish FSSAI recognised laboratories for conducting pre-import tests of the consignment in accordance with European Union Codex."

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food products standards and Food additives) Regulations 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. When the writ petition came up for hearing today, Sri.Sherry J. Thomas, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Additional Commissioner of Customs, Kochi has by order passed on 10.3.2014 permitted the petitioner to re-export the goods on payment of a fine of Rs.25,000/- under section 125 of the Customs Act, 1962 and also levied a fine of Rs.5,000/- under section 112(a) of the Customs Act, 1962 and therefore, the writ petition may be disposed of reserving liberty with the petitioner to challenge Ext.P11 report of analysis in other appropriate proceedings.
Sri .John Varghese, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the Central Board of Excise and Customs did not oppose the said submission.

entities.text: Central Board of Excise and Customs
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The writ petition is accordingly dismissed as withdrawn, reserving liberty with the petitioner to challenge the report of analysis in appeal before the competent authority as also the order passed by the Additional Commissioner of Customs if he is aggrieved thereby, in other appropriate proceedings.
The contentions raised by the petitioner on the merits are kept open.

Sd/-
P.N.RAVINDRAN JUDGE rkc/vpv
